issues.legal_issue: A settlement deed conferring substantially all of an infirm transferor’s property on a beneficiary is invalid when suspicious and unconscionable circumstances are not dispelled by proof of voluntary execution.
material_facts: The transferor was in his seventies, suffered from diabetes and other ailments, and was found to be in a state of senility and infirmity.

The beneficiary took the transferor to a nursing home, where the deed was executed and registered; the transferor’s wife testified that pressure was used while he was not fit to understand what he was doing.
The deed was prepared on instructions from the beneficiary’s friend, without the transferor’s consultation or approval of a draft.
The deed gave the beneficiary substantially all the transferor’s property, made only negligible provision for the transferor’s wife, and made no provision for his daughters or other grandchildren.

The beneficiary did not produce the nursing-home records or otherwise satisfactorily establish that the transferor executed the deed voluntarily, free from pressure or influence, and with awareness of its dispositions.
issues.conclusion: The deed of settlement was invalid; the appeal was allowed and the trial court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: When an unconscionable disposition and surrounding circumstances raise grave suspicion about execution, the burden shifts to the beneficiary to establish that the transferor executed the deed voluntarily, without external pressure or influence, while of sound mind and aware of the dispositions. No statutory provision or earlier case is cited in the judgment for this principle.

rule.if: challenge_to_settlement_deed and infirm_transferor and unconscionable_disposition and suspicious_execution_circumstances and beneficiary_failed_to_establish_voluntary_execution

predicates.challenge_to_settlement_deed: A party challenged the validity of a deed transferring property.
predicates.infirm_transferor: The transferor was elderly, ill, or mentally infirm when the deed was executed.
predicates.unconscionable_disposition: The deed made a substantially one-sided disposition of the transferor’s property.
predicates.suspicious_execution_circumstances: The circumstances of preparation or execution gave reason to doubt that the transferor acted freely and knowingly.
predicates.beneficiary_failed_to_establish_voluntar: The beneficiary did not adequately establish that the transferor executed the deed voluntarily, without pressure or influence, and with awareness of its dispositions.

issues.definition: When a challenged property-transfer deed involves an infirm transferor, a substantially one-sided disposition, and suspicious execution circumstances, it is invalid if the beneficiary fails to establish voluntary and informed execution.
